alba-0.name: Kenneth MacAlpin
alba-0.era: d. 858; king in the mid-ninth century
alba-0.attire: Wool tunic, linen underlayer, heavy muted green cloak fastened with an Insular silver penannular brooch; modest gold fillet
alba-0.props: Sheathed early medieval sword, small reliquary
alba-0.setting: Timber royal hall near Dunkeld, carved cross visible in rain beyond
alba-0.likeness: Invented mature face; no reliable life portrait. Royal chronology is evidence, while face and staging are reconstruction. Brooch follows surviving early medieval Scottish material culture, not a personal possession.
alba-0.avoid: Modern clan tartan, kilt, plate armour, Viking horned helmet, treating a later royal portrait as eyewitness evidence
alba-0.visualIdentity: Mid-ninth century; apparent age 50 is an invented casting choice because birth date is uncertain. Broad square face, heavy straight brows, deep-set eyes, coarse dark hair threaded with grey, close full beard; grounded and still. All facial details invented, not a recovered likeness.

alba-1.name: St Margaret
alba-1.attire: Late eleventh-century long wool/silk gown, restrained embroidered mantle, linen head veil and slim circlet
alba-1.props: Small decorated Gospel book held to chest
alba-1.setting: Quiet Romanesque royal chapel interior evoking Dunfermline
alba-1.likeness: Face interpreted, not a verified likeness. Piety and book patronage have textual evidence; Bodleian Gospel association supports the chosen prop. No assertion this imagined gown survives.
alba-1.avoid: Renaissance crown, late Gothic hennin, modern tartan, literal halo mistaken for physical attire
alba-1.visualIdentity: Circa 1080, about 35. Invented narrow oval face, fine straight brows, long nose and calm closed mouth, brown hair barely visible beneath veil. Distinct from the younger, rounder Matilda; no verified life likeness.
alba-1.artDirectionReview: Reconstruct a modest late-eleventh-century chapel, not the surviving twelfth-century Dunfermline nave or later Edinburgh chapel attributed to David I.

alba-2.name: Malcolm III
alba-2.attire: Eleventh-century mail shirt over quilted tunic; heavy wool cloak, narrow royal circlet
alba-2.props: Simple straight sword and edge of a kite shield
alba-2.setting: Windy Anglo-Scottish border fort with timber palisade
alba-2.likeness: Mature weathered face is reconstruction. The historical warrior king is distinct from Shakespeare's character; identity and frontier career are sourced.
alba-2.avoid: Shakespeare costume, modern great kilt, full plate, oversized fantasy blade
alba-2.visualIdentity: Circa 1080, about 49. Invented large broad head, strong cheek planes, broken-looking but not claimed injured nose, thick dark moustache and short salt-and-pepper beard, receding temples; robust mature build. No verified face.

alba-3.name: David I
alba-3.attire: Anglo-Norman long tunic, embroidered collar and restrained mantle; low open crown
alba-3.props: Rolled sealed charter, stone architectural plan suggested on desk
alba-3.setting: Romanesque abbey arcade beside an emerging burgh
alba-3.likeness: Interpretive face, based on twelfth-century royal types rather than claiming a life portrait. Abbey and charter staging evokes documented reforms.
alba-3.avoid: Renaissance scholar costume, spectacles, Gothic building completed centuries later
alba-3.visualIdentity: Circa 1140, about 56. Invented lean long face, high forehead, thin lips, swept-back greying hair and clean-shaven chin. Elderly scholarly bearing without spectacles. Facial choices are reconstruction.
alba-3.artDirectionReview: Generic Romanesque masonry is safer than copying later Melrose ruins. The source is biography, not evidence for a surviving garment or this architectural plan.

alba-4.name: William the Lion
alba-4.attire: Late twelfth-century mail hauberk, plain ochre surcoat and wool mantle; uncovered head with modest circlet
alba-4.props: Upright sheathed sword and small wax seal
alba-4.setting: Stone hall associated with Arbroath, early pointed arch
alba-4.likeness: No assured facial likeness; a deliberately individual adult reconstruction. Royal seal/royal biography supports rulership, not exact face or costume colours.
alba-4.avoid: Lion pelt, full fifteenth-century armour, pretending the nickname proves a personal lion garment
alba-4.visualIdentity: Circa 1195, about 53. Invented broad long face, weathered cheeks, greying sandy hair and short forked beard, steady deep-set gaze. Deliberately older and bearded beside clean-shaven Alexander II and III; no assured likeness or hair colour.
alba-4.artDirectionReview: Arbroath was founded during his reign; show modest late-twelfth-century work, not the fully developed surviving later medieval ruin or modern restoration.

alba-5.name: Alexander II
alba-5.attire: Thirteenth-century long tunic and fur-lined blue-green mantle; open crown
alba-5.setting: Border hall with hills beyond, recalling the 1237 Treaty of York
alba-5.likeness: Plausible mature face, not eyewitness portrait. Treaty, identity and dates are documented; setting and garment palette inferred.
alba-5.avoid: Russian imperial uniform or likeness of Tsar Alexander II; modern drawn national borders
alba-5.visualIdentity: At the 1237 Treaty of York, age 38–39. Invented narrow oval face, straight auburn hair ending at jaw, clean-shaven cheeks and chin, long straight nose and slight downward mouth corners. Hair colour and face are artistic choices, not historical facts.

alba-6.name: Alexander III
alba-6.attire: Rich mid-thirteenth-century tunic, crimson mantle fastened at shoulder, low crown
alba-6.props: Folded parchment and small royal seal
alba-6.setting: Scottish stone chamber opening onto a distant western sea
alba-6.likeness: Face reconstructed. Later manuscript royal imagery is iconographic context, not a photographic likeness; western-sea setting evokes the settlement of 1266.
alba-6.avoid: Tsar Alexander III, nineteenth-century uniforms, oversized modern Scottish regalia
alba-6.visualIdentity: At the 1266 settlement, about 25. Invented youthful full cheeks, broad short nose, clean-shaven face, thick dark softly wavy ear-length hair, upright relaxed bearing. Clearly younger and rounder than Alexander II; no verified likeness.

alba-7.name: Robert the Bruce
alba-7.attire: Early fourteenth-century mail with restrained coat of plates beneath surcoat, weathered cloak; head bare
alba-7.props: One-handed battle axe held low; shield edge
alba-7.setting: Bannockburn terrain with distant Stirling silhouette
alba-7.likeness: Interpretive face. Later statues and skull-derived reconstructions do not establish an exact life likeness; use the historical sites for context only.
alba-7.avoid: Blue face paint, kilt, late full plate, actor likeness, gore
alba-7.visualIdentity: Bannockburn period 1314, about 40. Invented angular compact face, close-cropped dark hair, short practical beard, pronounced cheekbones and determined closed mouth. Neither a film actor nor a claim to definitive skull reconstruction.
alba-7.artDirectionReview: Stirling background must be an indistinct medieval stronghold, not the present Renaissance palace, sixteenth-century Great Hall or later foreground defenses.

alba-8.name: Marjorie Bruce
alba-8.era: c. 1296–1316; daughter of Robert I, mother of Robert II
alba-8.attire: Early fourteenth-century long fitted-sleeve gown, light veil, narrow jeweled fillet; no sovereign crown
alba-8.props: Small folded family letter, simple girdle
alba-8.setting: Quiet western Scottish noble chamber, stone window and subdued tapestry
alba-8.likeness: Young adult reconstruction; no verified life likeness identified. She was a princess, not a reigning queen: Queen is a game role. HES documents her marriage to Walter and their royal son.
alba-8.avoid: Queen regnant regalia, Tudor hood, romanticized childbirth scene, claim that a later tomb effigy is certain
alba-8.visualIdentity: Circa 1315, about 19. Invented youthful heart-shaped face, soft broad cheekbones, straight brows, auburn-brown hair covered by veil. No adult age beyond her short life; individual features are invented.

alba-9.name: Robert II
alba-9.attire: Late fourteenth-century fur-lined mantle over fitted tunic, understated open crown
alba-9.likeness: Older king with silver hair, interpreted facial structure. Written age and succession history support an elderly portrayal; later portraits are not life evidence.
alba-9.avoid: Youthful warrior archetype, Tudor robes, literal sinister caricature from Intriguer role
alba-9.visualIdentity: Circa 1380, about 64. Invented heavy-lidded older face, broad nose, thinning white hair and close white beard, lined cheeks and substantial neck. Age grounded in chronology; not a youthful warrior or known exact likeness.
alba-9.artDirectionReview: Dundonald fourteenth-century hall is period-compatible; reconstruct a lived-in interior, not the modern roofless visitor-site ruin.

alba-10.name: Duncan I
alba-10.attire: Early eleventh-century wool tunic, simple woven cloak, mail only at neckline
alba-10.props: Spear upright to side, small plain brooch
alba-10.setting: Northern royal timber hall in cool morning light
alba-10.likeness: Adult face invented; chronology supported, exact appearance unknown. Avoid automatically presenting Shakespeare's elderly victim.
alba-10.avoid: Shakespeare elderly stage king, modern Highland uniform, plate armour
alba-10.visualIdentity: Circa 1038; invented apparent age early thirties, not a claim to precise birth date. Long clean-shaven face, strong rounded chin, dark short curls and alert wide eyes. Avoid Shakespeare elderly-victim casting.

alba-11.name: Donald II
alba-11.attire: Ninth-century dark wool tunic and earth-brown cloak pinned with an Insular brooch
alba-11.props: Simple sword hilt at belt, timber staff
alba-11.setting: Northern timber stronghold, distant coast and rain
alba-11.likeness: Distinct invented face. Thin documentary evidence supports only cautious early medieval reconstruction, not precise costume ownership or eye colour.
alba-11.avoid: Modern tartan, horned helmet, heraldic lion surcoat, castle from later Middle Ages
alba-11.visualIdentity: Circa 895; invented apparent age mid-forties because birth date is uncertain. Wide cheekbones, narrow chin, long dark moustache with otherwise shaved chin, straight shoulder-length dark hair. Deliberate invented identity, not documented grooming.

alba-12.name: Constantine II
alba-12.attire: Early tenth-century muted wool robe, mantle and restrained silver brooch
alba-12.props: Small cross and rolled ecclesiastical parchment
alba-12.setting: Royal assembly near a stone cross, low timber buildings
alba-12.likeness: Reconstructed elderly statesman; no contemporary facial likeness established. Source supports reign, while the assembly staging is artistic inference.
alba-12.avoid: Byzantine emperor Constantine, Roman laurel armour, modern kilt, Gothic script rendered as legible fact
alba-12.visualIdentity: Late reign circa 935; invented apparent age about 60, since exact birth date is uncertain. Thin triangular face, high domed forehead, sparse grey hair and long narrow silver beard; gentle tired eyes. Not an authenticated likeness.

alba-13.name: Matilda of Scotland
alba-13.era: c. 1080–1118; Edith, queen of Henry I from 1100
alba-13.attire: Early twelfth-century Anglo-Norman long gown, fine linen veil with narrow circlet, embroidered mantle
alba-13.props: Small devotional manuscript, folded court letter
alba-13.likeness: Invented adult likeness. Abbey evidence identifies Edith/Matilda and her marriage/regency; this is not Empress Matilda or Matilda of Flanders.
alba-13.avoid: Conflation with her daughter Empress Matilda, Tudor hood, Gothic hennin
alba-13.visualIdentity: Circa 1110, about 30. Invented rounder face than Margaret, softly arched brows, small firm chin, dark hair concealed under linen veil, engaged direct gaze. No verified portrait; not Empress Matilda.
alba-13.artDirectionReview: Use the eleventh-century Romanesque Westminster predecessor, not the extant thirteenth-century Gothic abbey or later towers.

habsburg-0.name: Rudolf I
habsburg-0.attire: Thirteenth-century long tunic, royal mantle and open crown
habsburg-0.likeness: Lean older face inspired cautiously by tomb-image tradition; not a photographic reconstruction. Institution records dates and kingship. Never crowned Holy Roman Emperor.
habsburg-0.avoid: Rudolf II Renaissance artist-emperor, Austrian imperial crown of 1602, full plate
habsburg-0.visualIdentity: Circa 1280, about 62. Tomb-image tradition suggests an older lean long face and strong nose; thinning grey hair and clean-shaven cheeks chosen as reconstruction. Exact living expression and hair uncertain.

habsburg-1.name: Maria Theresa
habsburg-1.attire: Mid-eighteenth-century silk court gown, lace sleeve ruffles, jeweled bodice and ermine mantle; modest powdered hair
habsburg-1.props: Folded state document, crown resting low on table
habsburg-1.setting: Viennese audience chamber with restrained gilded architecture
habsburg-1.likeness: Mature round-featured face guided by Meytens portrait tradition; a new interpretation rather than exact copy. She was sovereign of Habsburg lands and empress consort, not elected Holy Roman Emperor.
habsburg-1.avoid: Marie Antoinette's enormous later coiffure, medieval gown, all crowns merged into invented object
habsburg-1.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1750, about 33. Meytens portrait tradition: broad rounded face, arched brows, small mouth, full cheeks, powdered hair dressed low rather than towering. Mature sovereign and substantial figure, not generic elderly empress.

habsburg-2.name: Maximilian I
habsburg-2.attire: Black broad soft cap, rich fur-trimmed robe, Golden Fleece collar
habsburg-2.props: Pomegranate held low, manuscript at side
habsburg-2.setting: Early Renaissance imperial study with alpine window
habsburg-2.likeness: Use Dürer-derived long nose, shoulder-length grey hair and mature profile as portrait evidence; environment inferred. KHM explains propaganda and portrait variants.
habsburg-2.avoid: Giant fantasy armour, powdered wig, identical face to Charles V
habsburg-2.visualIdentity: Circa 1518, about 59. Dürer-derived long hooked nose, pursed lips, strong chin, shoulder-length grey hair and clean-shaven face. Distinctive older emperor, no invented beard.

habsburg-3.name: Charles V
habsburg-3.attire: Mid-sixteenth-century etched steel armour, muted red sash, Golden Fleece insignia
habsburg-3.props: Command baton, helmet low at side
habsburg-3.setting: Dusk beside military encampment with river and trees
habsburg-3.likeness: Titian portrait tradition informs reddish beard and long lower face; composition newly interpreted. Physical traits treated respectfully, not as caricature.
habsburg-3.avoid: Valois Charles V, eighteenth-century wig, exaggerated jaw, modern medals
habsburg-3.visualIdentity: 1547–1548, about 47–48. Titian-derived elongated face and lower jaw, short reddish beard, receding closely trimmed hair, serious tired eyes. Preserve recognizable proportions respectfully; avoid exaggerated Habsburg caricature.
habsburg-3.artDirectionReview: Prado object record now added as specific Titian evidence. Actual portrait uses a half-pike and pistol; a command baton is an optional new composition, not copied evidence. Armour dated mid-1540s.

habsburg-4.name: Philip I
habsburg-4.era: 1478–1506; Philip the Fair of Castile and Burgundy
habsburg-4.attire: Cloth-of-gold surcoat, dark fur collar, black soft cap and Golden Fleece
habsburg-4.props: Leather gloves and folded dynastic letter
habsburg-4.likeness: National Trust c.1495 panel describes fair shoulder-length hair and court dress. Show youthful adult with those traits; exact face remains painted interpretation.
habsburg-4.avoid: Philip II's ruff and black beard; Rubens later imagined armour treated as from life
habsburg-4.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1495, about 17. National Trust panel supports fair shoulder-length hair and youthful clean-shaven face; slender adolescent-to-young-adult cheeks, not mature bearded Philip II. New expression remains interpretation.

habsburg-5.name: Ferdinand I
habsburg-5.attire: Dark Renaissance robe and small cap, fur trim, short pale collar, Golden Fleece
habsburg-5.props: Administrative charter with hanging wax seal
habsburg-5.likeness: Long-nosed mature face from KHM portrait tradition; not Ferdinand I of nineteenth-century Austria. Documented government supports paper prop, not exact reconstruction of a meeting.
habsburg-5.avoid: Nineteenth-century Austrian uniform, brother Charles V's battlefield composition
habsburg-5.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1555, about 52. KHM portrait tradition: long narrow face, prominent straight nose, dark hair greying at temples, close beard and moustache. Keep older statesman bearing distinct from brother Charles V; reconstructed fine details.

habsburg-6.name: Philip II
habsburg-6.attire: Severe black Spanish court doublet, white standing ruff, Golden Fleece chain
habsburg-6.props: Folded dispatch and rosary held low
habsburg-6.setting: Austere stone chamber evoking El Escorial
habsburg-6.likeness: Anguissola 1573 portrait supplies pale mature face and short beard; setting is artistic interpretation. Black dress communicates documented court fashion, not moral villainy.
habsburg-6.avoid: Victorian black suit, fantasy assassin props, excessive black eyeliner
habsburg-6.visualIdentity: 1573, about 46. Anguissola type: pale narrow mature face, receding light-brown hair, short carefully trimmed beard and moustache, heavy-lidded measured gaze. Not a black-bearded villain.
habsburg-6.artDirectionReview: El Escorial was under construction in 1573: use a plain granite room, no claim that the completed later decorative programme already existed.

habsburg-7.name: Anna of Austria
habsburg-7.era: 1549–1580; Philip II's fourth wife, queen of Spain
habsburg-7.attire: 1570s Spanish court gown, fitted jeweled bodice, white ruff, neatly arranged light hair with pearls
habsburg-7.props: Fine gloves held low, small jewel pendant
habsburg-7.setting: Madrid Alcázar audience chamber, dark restrained backdrop
habsburg-7.likeness: Explicit identity decision: Prado's Anguissola portrait of Ana (1573), not Anne of France 1601–1666. Portrait guides youthful features and coiffure; room and pose newly invented.
habsburg-7.avoid: Conflation with Bourbon Anne, seventeenth-century lace collar or wide panniers
habsburg-7.visualIdentity: 1573, about 24. Anguissola type: youthful elongated oval face, broad clear forehead, fine brows, small closed mouth and light dressed hair. No resemblance swap with much older Bourbon Anne regent.

habsburg-8.name: Margaret of Austria
habsburg-8.attire: Widow's dark square-neck gown over plain chemisette, folded linen cap and beaded necklace
habsburg-8.setting: Mechelen library with discreet books and cabinet
habsburg-8.likeness: Conrad Meit's court portrait bust supports adult features and precisely described dress. Regent identity distinguishes her from Margaret 1584–1611, queen of Spain. Setting inferred from court patronage.
habsburg-8.avoid: Childhood betrothal portrait as adult likeness, Spanish queen on horseback, poison bottle
habsburg-8.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1520, about 40. Meit bust supports broad oval face, substantial cheeks, small lips and steady gaze within folded linen cap. Mature widow-regent, not Met childhood portrait aged only by adding wrinkles.

habsburg-9.name: Ferdinand II
habsburg-9.attire: Blackened early seventeenth-century armour, white lace collar, Golden Fleece
habsburg-9.props: Command baton and helmet on ledge
habsburg-9.setting: Imperial chamber with dark curtain and architectural column
habsburg-9.likeness: KHM Georg Pachmann c.1635 portrait provides mature bearded face and black armour. This is the emperor, not Ferdinand II of Tyrol (1529–1595).
habsburg-9.avoid: Tyrolean archduke's 1550s slashed silver doublet, fantasy religious villain iconography
habsburg-9.visualIdentity: Circa 1635, about 57. Pachmann portrait tradition: broad mature face, receding dark greying hair, thick moustache and neat pointed beard; lined forehead. Different from the young Tyrolean archduke.

habsburg-10.name: Leopold I
habsburg-10.attire: Late seventeenth-century black armour, lace neckcloth, dark curled full-bottom wig and Golden Fleece
habsburg-10.props: Baton, low sheet of music as secondary detail
habsburg-10.likeness: Benjamin von Block c.1672 portrait guides long face, moustache and wig. Portray distinctive facial structure without mocking exaggeration; music refers to documented interest.
habsburg-10.avoid: Belgian Leopold I, nineteenth-century uniform, exaggerated genetic caricature
habsburg-10.visualIdentity: Circa 1672, about 32. Benjamin von Block type: elongated face, pronounced lower lip/jaw, thin moustache, dark long curled wig. Young mature ruler despite wig; no grotesque exaggeration.

habsburg-11.name: Charles VI
habsburg-11.attire: Early eighteenth-century formal coat with rich embroidery, dark curled wig and Golden Fleece insignia
habsburg-11.props: Sealed succession document evoking Pragmatic Sanction
habsburg-11.setting: Viennese council room with restrained Baroque column
habsburg-11.likeness: Institutional c.1720/30 and Auerbach portraits anchor mature facial type. Document prop derives from succession policy; no fabricated readable decree.
habsburg-11.avoid: French Valois Charles VI, Joseph II military austerity, giant modern eagle emblem
habsburg-11.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1730, about 45. Institutional portrait tradition: long mature face, prominent nose and lower lip, dark curled full wig, clean-shaven cheeks. Formal closed mouth, distinct from Joseph II short powdered hairstyle.

habsburg-12.name: Joseph II
habsburg-12.attire: Restrained eighteenth-century military uniform coat, waistcoat, white neckcloth, powdered short tied hair
habsburg-12.setting: Plain working desk in an imperial room, daylight
habsburg-12.likeness: Portrait tradition guides mature broad forehead and unshowy bearing. Institutional evidence supports admission of uniforms at court and administrative reform; details of this desk are inferred.
habsburg-12.avoid: Napoleonic medals, oversized Baroque wig, medieval crown worn with uniform
habsburg-12.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1780, about 39. Portrait-informed broad forehead, receding hairline under short powdered tied hair, full nose, clean-shaven cheeks and firm mouth. Working adult ruler, not elderly general; exact expression inferred.

habsburg-13.name: Mary of Hungary
habsburg-13.era: 1505–1558; widowed queen and governor of Netherlands
habsburg-13.attire: Severe mid-sixteenth-century widow's dark gown, close white cap and dark veil
habsburg-13.props: Folded diplomatic letter and small seal
habsburg-13.setting: Brussels governmental chamber with a subdued sculptural niche
habsburg-13.likeness: Leone Leoni's c.1555 bust commissioned within her dynastic portrait programme informs mature face and widow's silhouette. Do not substitute Maria Anna of Spain (1606–1646).
habsburg-13.avoid: Seventeenth-century Spanish infanta hairstyle, Anne of Austria confusion, generic young queen
habsburg-13.visualIdentity: Circa 1555, about 50. Leoni bust supports mature elongated face and sharp straight nose framed by close widow headwear, thin lips, restrained gaze. Hair concealed, age visible, not a young Spanish infanta.

plantagenet-0.name: Henry II
plantagenet-0.era: c.1170, Angevin England and western France
plantagenet-0.attire: Long wool tunic, patterned silk mantle, narrow belt and low open crown.
plantagenet-0.props: Rolled writ and plain sword hilt.
plantagenet-0.setting: Romanesque hall at Chinon, limestone arch.
plantagenet-0.likeness: Fontevraud effigy supplies royal costume context; mature compact face and reddish beard are interpretive, not a proven portrait.
plantagenet-0.avoid: No full plate armour or Renaissance ruff.
plantagenet-0.visualIdentity: Circa 1170, about 37. Compact broad face, heavy neck, short reddish beard and receding reddish hair are reconstruction choices here, not certified by the effigy. Distinct from tall lean Richard.
plantagenet-0.artDirectionReview: Chinon setting is an evocation of a twelfth-century hall, not an exact reconstruction or later château façade.

plantagenet-1.name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
plantagenet-1.attire: Long fitted gown, pale veil under crown, rich mantle.
plantagenet-1.props: Open illuminated book, held below chest.
plantagenet-1.setting: Romanesque abbey arcade with warm Aquitaine light.
plantagenet-1.likeness: Reading pose derives from her Fontevraud effigy; facial individuality is reconstructed rather than claimed as a life likeness.
plantagenet-1.avoid: No exposed fantasy corset, hennin or Tudor hood.
plantagenet-1.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1190, about 68. Elderly long oval face with fine wrinkles, firm mouth and grey hair mostly hidden by veil. Effigy guides the reading pose and courtly silhouette, not facial accuracy; do not default to a twenty-year-old queen.

plantagenet-2.name: Richard I
plantagenet-2.attire: Mail hauberk and coif lowered around neck, simple surcoat and mantle.
plantagenet-2.props: Straight sword and shield at lower side.
plantagenet-2.setting: Stone coastal fortress with distant Mediterranean light, an interpretive crusading setting.
plantagenet-2.likeness: Fontevraud effigy is commemorative evidence, not an exact life portrait; use a mature bearded face.
plantagenet-2.avoid: No late-medieval plate harness, horned helmet or modern national flag.
plantagenet-2.visualIdentity: Circa 1192, about 35. Invented long rectangular face, long straight nose, closely trimmed tawny beard and shoulder-length tawny hair; tall upright bearing. Commemorative effigy is not proof of these exact colours/features.

plantagenet-3.name: John
plantagenet-3.attire: Rich long tunic, mantle, small open crown.
plantagenet-3.props: Great seal beside a rolled charter.
plantagenet-3.likeness: Worcester preserves an early royal effigy; use its crowned, bearded convention without asserting portrait accuracy.
plantagenet-3.avoid: Show a sealed charter, not John signing Magna Carta with a modern pen.
plantagenet-3.visualIdentity: Circa 1215, about 48. Rounded middle-aged face, high forehead, short curled beard with a little grey and medium dark wavy hair. These are interpretive variations on effigy convention, not an authenticated living likeness.

plantagenet-4.name: Henry III
plantagenet-4.attire: Long ceremonial robe with narrow trim, mantle, open crown.
plantagenet-4.setting: Westminster Gothic building works suggested through an arch.
plantagenet-4.likeness: Abbey burial and rebuilding are documented; live facial modelling is interpretive, informed by his effigy.
plantagenet-4.avoid: No Tudor rose, full plate armour or completed modern Abbey skyline.
plantagenet-4.visualIdentity: Circa 1265, about 58. Invented slim older face, slightly asymmetrical brows, straight nose, short greying beard and thin greying hair; attentive architectural-patron bearing. Effigy supplies iconographic context.
plantagenet-4.artDirectionReview: Westminster should be under construction in the 1260s; omit eighteenth-century west towers and nineteenth-century Parliament.

plantagenet-5.name: Edward I
plantagenet-5.attire: Mail with modest reinforcing plates, crimson mantle; tall restrained silhouette.
plantagenet-5.likeness: Abbey account records red-and-gold royal burial dress and crimson mantle; living face is reconstructed.
plantagenet-5.avoid: No Gothic full plate harness or literal war hammer from later epithet.
plantagenet-5.visualIdentity: Circa 1295, about 56. Tall lean silhouette, long face, prominent nose, shoulder-length silver-brown hair and close grey beard. Living face is invented; burial evidence does not certify hair colour or exact facial structure.

plantagenet-6.name: Edward II
plantagenet-6.attire: Long silk robe, mantle and open leaf crown.
plantagenet-6.likeness: Gloucester alabaster effigy provides commemorative reference; soft individual facial features are interpretive.
plantagenet-6.avoid: No feminizing caricature or execution imagery.
plantagenet-6.visualIdentity: Circa 1318, about 34. Invented broad smooth forehead, full lips, strong rounded chin, clean-shaven cheeks and softly waved brown jaw-length hair. Mature adult, not a child or effeminized caricature; effigy-informed convention only.

plantagenet-7.name: Edward III
plantagenet-7.attire: Mid-fourteenth-century transitional armour with mail at joints; restrained royal mantle.
plantagenet-7.likeness: Abbey bronze shows long hair and beard; adapt mature features rather than copy the late-life death-mask expression.
plantagenet-7.avoid: No sixteenth-century armour; no three-lily French quartering for this date.
plantagenet-7.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1355, about 43. Long face and flowing dark hair with substantial pointed beard echo tomb convention; living expression and hair colour reconstructed. Broader shoulders than Richard II, no late-life death-mask look.
plantagenet-7.artDirectionReview: Use generic fourteenth-century Windsor masonry; omit nineteenth-century rebuilt skyline and later St George chapel.

plantagenet-8.name: Philippa of Hainault
plantagenet-8.attire: Reticulated headdress, fitted laced bodice, buttoned sleeves and loose mantle.
plantagenet-8.props: One hand on cloak cord; small closed book.
plantagenet-8.setting: Windsor chamber with Flemish woven hanging.
plantagenet-8.likeness: Her Westminster alabaster effigy supplies a full face and substantial figure; mature warmth is an artistic interpretation.
plantagenet-8.avoid: No slim generic maiden, Tudor hood or horned hennin.
plantagenet-8.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1355, about 41. Full broad face and substantial mature figure following alabaster effigy, small mouth and soft cheeks; hair hidden by veil. Natural mature woman, not a generic slim young queen.

plantagenet-9.name: Richard II
plantagenet-9.attire: Rich patterned robe, fine open crown, white-hart jewel.
plantagenet-9.likeness: Wilton Diptych provides contemporary idealized royal image and white-hart symbolism; preserve slender youthful countenance without treating it as photography.
plantagenet-9.avoid: No battle armour, sinister caricature or later Tudor ornament.
plantagenet-9.visualIdentity: Circa 1395, about 28. Contemporary Wilton image supports slender youthful royal type: elongated oval face, fine brows, smooth pale cheeks and auburn hair; light fine facial hair only if following that iconography. Idealized portrait, not photographic certainty.

plantagenet-10.name: Edward the Black Prince
plantagenet-10.attire: Fourteenth-century plate elements over mail, short heraldic jupon.

plantagenet-10.visualIdentity: Circa 1365, about 35. Invented narrow athletic face, strong straight brow, thick dark hair and a neat short moustache with close chin beard. Armour evidence is firmer than the reconstructed living face. Not black skin or black-painted face derived from epithet.

plantagenet-11.name: Joan of Kent
plantagenet-11.attire: Silk fitted gown, fine veil and modest jeweled fillet.
plantagenet-11.props: Silver cup held below portrait center.
plantagenet-11.likeness: IHR records her marriage, Aquitaine household and silver vessels; face, exact dress and room are explicitly plausible reconstruction.

plantagenet-11.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1370, about 42. Invented broad heart-shaped face, long nose, full lips, auburn-brown hair mostly concealed, mature composed gaze. Exact features unknown; avoid generic youthful bride despite marriage role.

plantagenet-12.name: Geoffrey of Anjou
plantagenet-12.era: c.1140, Anjou and Maine; Geoffrey V, Henry II's father

plantagenet-12.visualIdentity: Circa 1140, about 27. Slender youthful face, short neat beard, straight brown hair to ears; colouring and realism invented around stylized enamel reference. No middle-aged generic monarch.

plantagenet-13.name: Isabella of France

plantagenet-13.avoid: No wolf pelt or villain stereotype; epithet is later hostile rhetoric.

plantagenet-13.artDirectionReview: Eltham means medieval royal manor context; no surviving Tudor great hall treated as built in 1325, no twentieth-century Art Deco palace.

tudor-0.name: Henry VII

tudor-0.visualIdentity: Circa 1505, about 48. NPG portrait tradition: narrow long face, high cheekbones, thin firm mouth, long nose, dark greying straight hair under cap, clean-shaven. Reserved middle-aged bearing; setting and micro-expression inferred.

tudor-1.name: Elizabeth I
tudor-1.attire: Jeweled gown, lace ruff, pearls and dressed red hair.

tudor-1.likeness: Darnley portrait tradition supplies recognizable long face; generated skin and expression remain interpretation.

tudor-1.visualIdentity: Circa 1575, about 42. Darnley portrait tradition: long pale oval face, high forehead, fine arched brows, reddish curled hair, narrow mouth. A mature queen, not teenage beauty; age lines restrained by idealized court portrait conventions.

tudor-2.name: Henry VIII
tudor-2.attire: Broad fur-trimmed gown, slashed doublet, jeweled flat bonnet, gold chain.

tudor-2.visualIdentity: Circa 1540, about 49. Holbein-derived broad nearly square face, small eyes, compact reddish beard, broad neck and imposing substantial shoulders. Keep unmistakably different from Henry VII; no generic lean warrior.

tudor-3.name: Mary I
tudor-3.attire: Pearl-edged headdress, patterned gown and purple overgown.

tudor-4.name: Edward VI
tudor-4.attire: High-collared embroidered doublet, short cloak, jeweled cap.

tudor-4.visualIdentity: Circa 1550, about 13. Smooth adolescent oval face, small chin, light straight hair and clean-shaven cheeks; slender boy shoulders. Royal portrait evidence supplies youthful proportions; never an adult bearded Lawgiver.

tudor-5.name: Elizabeth of York
tudor-5.attire: Early Tudor gable hood, rich square-neck gown, jeweled edging.

tudor-5.avoid: No Elizabeth I ruff or elaborate late-century hair.
tudor-5.visualIdentity: Circa 1500, about 34. Later portrait tradition: pale oval face, softly pointed chin, fine brows, small closed lips and hair largely hidden by gable hood. Treat facial specifics as interpretation from copies, not direct sitting.

tudor-6.name: Margaret Beaufort
tudor-6.attire: Black vowess gown, white linen wimple and dark hood.

tudor-6.avoid: Not a nun, witch or seductive intriguer; avoid invented sinister props.
tudor-6.visualIdentity: Circa 1505, about 62. Older narrow lined face, high cheekbones, thin mouth, hair entirely hidden by white vowess headwear. Posthumous portrait tradition supports older devotional silhouette, not photographic precision.

tudor-7.name: Edmund Tudor
tudor-7.era: c.1455, England and southwest Wales; Earl of Richmond
tudor-7.attire: Mid-fifteenth-century doublet and fur-edged gown, soft cap.

tudor-7.visualIdentity: Circa 1455, about 25. Invented smooth elongated face, strong brow, dark straight jaw-length hair, clean-shaven cheeks and chin, slim shoulders. No secure life portrait; not a later infant Edmund Tudor.

tudor-9.name: Margaret Tudor
tudor-9.attire: Early-sixteenth-century royal gown, jeweled hood, rich mantle.
tudor-9.setting: Scottish palace stone chamber, restrained thistle detail.
tudor-9.likeness: Royal Collection Mytens-derived image is later evidence, not a contemporary likeness; facial specificity is cautious reconstruction.
tudor-9.avoid: Do not use NPG 1173, now identified as an unknown woman; no tartan clan costume.
tudor-9.visualIdentity: Circa 1515, about 26. Cautious reconstruction: broad oval face, high forehead, soft pointed chin, reddish-brown hair almost hidden by hood. Later portrait evidence cannot certify precise youthful facial details.

tudor-10.name: Mary Tudor of France
tudor-10.attire: Early French court silk gown, jeweled hood, delicate gold necklace.

tudor-10.visualIdentity: 1514–1515, about 18–19. Invented youthful rounded oval face, full lower lip, delicate straight nose and fair reddish hair framed by early hood. Clear age and face distinction from her niece Mary I at 38; exact likeness unestablished here.

tudor-11.name: Arthur Tudor
tudor-11.era: c.1500, England; adolescent Prince of Wales
tudor-11.attire: Embroidered early Tudor doublet and modest dark cap.
tudor-11.likeness: NPG exhibition records Wewyck portrait made during marriage negotiations and its flower; depict a slight teenage boy.
tudor-11.avoid: Never an adult warrior or crowned king; no late-sixteenth-century costume.
tudor-11.visualIdentity: Circa 1500, about 14. Wewyck-associated portrait tradition: slight adolescent face, slim nose, small chin, auburn/light brown straight hair under cap, entirely clean-shaven. Boy proportions, not adult warrior prince.

tudor-12.name: Owen Tudor
tudor-12.era: c.1430–1440, Welsh courtier in English royal household
tudor-12.attire: Modest wool gown over fitted doublet, soft chaperon.
tudor-12.likeness: National Library of Wales establishes courtier identity and notes obscure early life; face, exact dress and pose are reconstructed.
tudor-12.avoid: No Tudor royal crown, union rose, caricatured Celtic warrior or secret-dagger stereotype.
tudor-12.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1435; invented apparent age mid-thirties, birth uncertain. Invented compact broad face, slightly rounded nose, thick dark straight hair to ears, clean-shaven chin and strong neck. No claimed life likeness or ethnic facial stereotype.

tudor-13.name: Catherine of Aragon
tudor-13.era: c.1525, English queen of Castilian-Aragonese origins
tudor-13.attire: Jeweled gable hood, rich gown with square neckline and fine linen.
tudor-13.props: Small prayer book with pomegranate decoration.
tudor-13.likeness: Prefer NPG c.1520 panel and Horenbout miniature tradition; distinguish them from NPG 163, an eighteenth-century copy. Face is interpreted from accepted portrait types.
tudor-13.avoid: No exoticized Spanish costume, flamenco mantilla or confusion with Mary Tudor of France.
tudor-13.visualIdentity: Circa 1525, about 40. Accepted portrait types: mature oval face, softly full cheeks, small firm mouth and auburn hair mostly concealed by hood. Do not infer black hair from Spanish origin; exact colour and face remain interpreted.

valois-0.name: Philip VI
valois-0.attire: Reconstructed long blue wool/silk royal robe, ermine-edged mantle, low open fleur-de-lis crown; early fourteenth-century silhouette.
valois-0.props: Small sceptre and sealed charter at lower edge.
valois-0.setting: Interpretive Gothic royal chamber with stone lancet window, not Versailles.
valois-0.likeness: The Saint-Denis effigy is documented by the French heritage inventory; use its idealized medieval convention, not a claim to certain facial likeness. Mature face and shoulder-length hair are reconstruction.
valois-0.avoid: Renaissance slashed doublet; late full plate harness; modern three-fleur arms replacing the earlier semy without explanation.
valois-0.visualIdentity: Circa 1340, about 47. Invented long narrow face, high forehead, swept-back greying dark hair and a neatly divided medium beard. Effigy is idealized, so no claim to exact facial likeness.

valois-1.name: Francis I
valois-1.attire: Broad black-and-cream slashed silk doublet, large sleeves, soft dark feathered cap, gold chain; French Renaissance court dress.

valois-2.name: Catherine de’ Medici

valois-2.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1570, about 51. Mature broad face, heavy-lidded eyes, short firm mouth, high forehead entirely framed by widow veil. Portrait-informed, neither glamorous young bride nor witch caricature.

valois-3.name: Charles V
valois-3.attire: Long fitted-sleeve robe, fur-lined mantle and modest open crown; fourteenth-century court silhouette.
valois-3.props: Illuminated bound manuscript held against chest.

valois-3.visualIdentity: Circa 1370, about 32. Individualized effigy informs thin elongated face, prominent nose, slight pointed beard and composed expression; paint dark straight hair and realistic skin as interpretation. Young mature scholar, not an old sage.

valois-4.name: Charles VII

valois-7.name: Charles IX

valois-9.name: Marguerite de Valois

bourbon-0.name: Henry IV

bourbon-1.name: Louis XIV

bourbon-2.name: Louis XIII

bourbon-4.name: Louis XV

bourbon-4.visualIdentity: 1763, about 53. Van Loo portrait tradition: mature oval face, prominent straight nose, firm thin mouth, clean-shaven cheeks and powdered side curls. Do not copy Louis XVI youthful broad cheeks.

bourbon-5.name: Louis XVI

bourbon-6.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1784, about 29. Portrait tradition: elongated oval face, high forehead, fair powdered hair, arched brows and small composed mouth. Mature adult in modest dressed hair, not a teenage bridal doll.

bourbon-7.name: Marie de’ Medici
bourbon-7.attire: Rich dark silk gown, structured bodice, broad lace collar and pearl jewels; early Baroque court silhouette.
bourbon-7.props: Folded architectural drawing near lower edge.
bourbon-7.setting: Interpretive Luxembourg Palace gallery with warm marble.
bourbon-7.likeness: Louvre preserves her portrait and Rubens cycle, evidence for her represented mature face and patronage. The architectural prop and realistic room recompose this evidence; no allegorical deities.
bourbon-7.avoid: Catherine de' Medici's sixteenth-century widow hood as interchangeable identity; Roman goddess armor treated as daily attire.
bourbon-7.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1622, about 49. Rubens/Pourbus portrait tradition: broad rounded face, high forehead, dark brows, substantial cheeks, brown hair dressed close beneath ornaments. Mature patron, not Catherine de Medici widow type.
bourbon-7.artDirectionReview: Chosen 1622 Luxembourg setting should be a recently built/in-progress patronage interior; do not show the completed Rubens cycle installed before 1625 or modern Senate fittings.

bourbon-8.name: Philippe of Orléans
bourbon-8.attire: Elaborately embroidered seventeenth-century coat, fine lace cravat, dark curled wig, jeweled order ornament.
bourbon-8.setting: Interpretive Saint-Cloud salon with a garden glimpse.
bourbon-8.likeness: Versailles explicitly identifies Louis XIV's brother Monsieur and his Saint-Cloud court. Facial rendering is interpretation informed by the period portrait tradition; this is not the later Regent Philippe II (1674–1723).
bourbon-8.avoid: Regent identity swap; mockery or stereotyped costume based on sexuality; eighteenth-century powdered wig.
bourbon-8.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1675, about 35. Cautious portrait-tradition reconstruction: smooth oval face, dark almond-shaped eyes, prominent straight nose, full lips and dark curled wig. No exact certified likeness from contextual biography; no sexuality-based caricature.
bourbon-8.artDirectionReview: Saint-Cloud is a reconstructed seventeenth-century salon, not a present-day surviving interior; contextual source supports court association, not exact face.

bourbon-9.name: Louis II de Condé
bourbon-9.attire: Seventeenth-century cuirass, white lace collar and red drapery; long natural or lightly dressed dark hair.
bourbon-9.setting: Interpretive distant campaign plain or Chantilly terrace, not nineteenth-century rebuilt château facade.
bourbon-9.likeness: Chantilly identifies Juste d'Egmont's portrait of the Grand Condé, with long hair and red drapery. Prominent aquiline nose and lean face are portrait-informed interpretation.
bourbon-9.avoid: Medieval plate suit; eighteenth-century tricorne; invented trophies of violence.
bourbon-9.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1655, about 34. Egmont portrait tradition: very prominent aquiline nose, lean long face, intense eyes, fine moustache and long dark hair. Deliberately angular and recognizably different from Louis XIII.
bourbon-9.artDirectionReview: Chantilly terrace must not use the nineteenth-century rebuilt château façade; generic campaign view is safest.

bourbon-10.name: Antoine of Bourbon
bourbon-10.attire: Refined dark doublet, small white neck frill, soft dark toque and fine gold chain.
bourbon-10.setting: Interpretive Renaissance Pau chamber with mountain light.
bourbon-10.likeness: Pau's 1557 François Clouet portrait is a contemporary source, described as a three-quarter view with penetrating gaze and refined severe costume. Short beard and facial proportions should follow this model.
bourbon-10.avoid: Henry IV's gray beard; seventeenth-century lace collar; folk Basque costume imposed on a French court prince.
bourbon-10.visualIdentity: 1557, about 39. Clouet source: narrow mature face, strong nose, penetrating eyes, close dark beard and moustache beneath soft cap. Not son Henry IV older grey-bearded image.

bourbon-11.name: Jeanne d’Albret
bourbon-11.attire: Restrained dark court gown, white linen neck frill, close dark hood and limited jewelry.
bourbon-11.props: Small bound French-language religious book with no invented readable scripture.
bourbon-11.setting: Interpretive Pau cabinet, plain timber table and Pyrenean daylight.
bourbon-11.likeness: Musée protestant documents her 1560 conversion and independent rule; Pau documents her portrait and enamel collections. Facial details and precise costume are cautious reconstruction, not a verified sitting.
bourbon-11.avoid: Puritan costume from seventeenth-century New England; nun's habit; poison-glove legend.
bourbon-11.visualIdentity: Circa 1565, about 37. Cautious reconstruction: long slim face, high forehead, narrow mouth, dark hair concealed by hood and concentrated gaze. Contextual sources do not certify the exact facial details.

bourbon-12.name: Philip V of Spain
bourbon-12.attire: Armor beneath embroidered coat, red waist sash, Golden Fleece and blue Saint-Esprit sash; curled wig.
bourbon-12.props: Ruler's baton with helmet low at side.
bourbon-12.setting: Interpretive Spanish royal stone terrace, not flamenco or bullfighting scenery.
bourbon-12.likeness: Prado's Jean Ranc official portrait of 1723 explicitly documents armor, baton, helmet, embroidered coat and both orders. Recompose its mature long face and courtly stance into the card crop.
bourbon-12.avoid: Philip IV Velázquez moustache/black golilla costume; modern Spanish flag; seventeenth-century Habsburg identity.
bourbon-12.visualIdentity: 1723, about 40. Ranc portrait type: elongated face, prominent nose, closed lips, clean-shaven jaw, abundant powdered-to-grey curled wig. No Philip IV thin moustache or Habsburg beard.
bourbon-12.artDirectionReview: 1723 Madrid royal backdrop must evoke the old Alcázar or a generic period terrace, not the present Royal Palace built after 1734.

bourbon-13.name: Louis XVIII
bourbon-13.attire: Dark high-collared embroidered coat, white stock, royal sash and period order star; short gray hair.
bourbon-13.props: Folded charter or dispatch resting on table.
bourbon-13.setting: Interpretive Restoration palace study, not a claim that he resumed residence at Versailles.
bourbon-13.likeness: Versailles documents his Restoration and Guérin's 1820 portrait. Elderly broad face and substantial build are portrait-informed; charter pose is interpretation. Versailles also says he abandoned plans to return there.
bourbon-13.avoid: Louis XIV wig; medieval costume; implying an actual coronation, which never occurred; caricaturing body size.
bourbon-13.visualIdentity: Choose circa 1818, about 63. Guérin/Restoration portrait tradition: broad elderly face, substantial cheeks and neck, short grey hair, clean-shaven chin and heavy-lidded eyes. Respectful likeness, no caricature.
bourbon-13.artDirectionReview: Restoration palace study is generic; not a claim Louis XVIII returned to live at Versailles.
